newsitem.title: JAPAN: DKB no comment on reported loans to Nomura client.
newsitem.headline: DKB no comment on reported loans to Nomura client.

text.p: Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB) said on Monday that it would not comment on a Japanese newspaper report over the weekend that it had lent some five billion yen to a company run by a relative of a "sokaiya" racketeer.

Japanese prosecutors and officials of the nation's securities watchdog have been investigating whether the same racketeer-linked firm had received illegal payments from directors of Nomura Securities Co Ltd.

Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported on Sunday that DKB has given up on recovering some three billion yen after the company paid back two billion yen. The loans were made in the year ended March 31, 1995.
It also said that a financial firm affiliated with DKB also lent some two billion yen to the company, most of which has been irrecoverable.
"We don't have any comment on this," a company spokesman said. He also said that the bank does not confirm the identity of firms to which it has made loans.
The newspaper said that prosecutors are investigating whether there is a link between DKB's loans and Nomura's irregular payment to the company.

The Nomura scandal surfaced on March 6 when the company, Japan's biggest brokerage, said internal probes found that the directors had made improper deals and funnelled profits raised through stock trading to a corporate client.
